RECHECK_INPUT.trigger: A bounded Opus recheck of v1.0.4 returned V104_BOUNDED_RECHECK_FAIL with exactly ONE blocking finding: v1.0.4 correctly reclassified the SEMANTIC_SWEEP_CLASSIFICATION table's SEVERITY.escalation_rule entry as an out-of-pattern direct-read finding, but the SAME false provenance claim survives, untouched, at a DIFFERENT locus in the SAME v1.0.3 document — CHEAP_ADDITIONAL_CLEANUPS.SEVERITY_ESCALATION_RULE_CLOSED.defect, whose text still reads '...This is a genuine gap the pattern sweep surfaced: found, not previously named by any round.'

self_diagnosis.what_went_wrong: v1.0.4 corrected the false provenance claim exactly once, at the locus its own SWEEP_METHOD_CORRECTED block was built to fix (the SEMANTIC_SWEEP_CLASSIFICATION hit table). It did not separately check whether the SAME sentence, or a paraphrase of it, existed anywhere ELSE in the same source document. v1.0.3's CHEAP_ADDITIONAL_CLEANUPS block, where the escalation-rule correction was ORIGINALLY authored, still carries its own defect-justification text asserting sweep discovery — a second, independent locus of the identical false claim that v1.0.4 never inspected because it was reasoning about the sweep table specifically, not about every place the phrase 'pattern sweep' appears.
self_diagnosis.generalisation: Correcting a false claim at the locus where a reviewer NAMED it is not the same as correcting every locus where the SAME document independently asserts it. This is the fourth time this exact defect class has recurred in this lineage (parent JSON vs. companion .md in v1.0.1->v1.0.2; a JSON field vs. its .md twin in v1.0.2->v1.0.3; a hand-enumerated precedence list vs. structural coverage in v1.0.3->v1.0.4; now a sweep-table entry vs. the original authoring block's own justification text in v1.0.4->v1.0.5). The recurring fix is the same each time: after closing a NAMED locus, grep the exact phrase — not a paraphrase, the literal string — across every file in the lineage before declaring the round closed. This round performed that grep as its first step and found exactly one surviving hit, confirming both the defect and that no second hidden restatement exists.
